With  Mr. C.V.S Shekhawat For Respondent(s) : Mr. V.S. Rajpurohit, PP _____________________________________________________  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAY BISHNOI Judgment / Order 10/01/2017 This Criminal Misc. Petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C is filed by the petitioner being aggrieved with the order dated 04.08.2012 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhilwara in criminal reference No.540/2003 whereby cognizance has been taken against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that the sample of the alleged adulterated edible oil was taken by the food inspector from the dealer in the year 1995.

It is alleged in the complaint that the sample of the said edible oil collected from the (2 of 3) [CRLMP-2656/2012] shop of Chhogalal S/o Banshilal situated at Station Road, Bhilwara was found adulterated on its examination.
It is alleged that the said edible oil was manufactured and supplied by the Tilam Sangh, Jaipur.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that as a matter of fact for the first time the petitioner was posted as a Managing Director of Tilam Sangh, Jaipur, after 2012.

It is also contended that earlier, the trial court took cognizance against two former Managing Directors of Tilam Sangh, Jaipur on 10.07.1996 and 18.04.2006, however, this Court in S.B. Criminal Misc.
Petition No.264/1999 decided on 19.12.2000 and S.B. Criminal Misc. Petition No.1347/2006 decided on 21.08.2007 has quashed the order of taking cognizance taking against two former Managing Directors of Tilam Sangh on the ground that at the time of taking sample of edible oil i.e.
on 15.09.1995, those Managing Directors were not posted and working at Tilam Sangh.
Learned Khem Raj vs State on 10 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125504913/

sentences.text: 1 counsel for the petitioner has argued that the case of the petitioner is also similar to that of those former Managing Directors of Tilam Sangh because the petitioner was also not working as a Managing Director on the date when the sample of edible oil were taken by the Food Inspector.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has therefore prayed that the order of taking cognizance be quashed.

Learned Public Prosecutor has oppsed the prayer of the petitioner, however, not in a position to dispute the fact that at the time of taking sample of the edible oil i.e. on 15.09.1995 the petitioner was not working as a Managing Director of Tilam Sangh, Jaipur.

[CRLMP-2656/2012] In view of the above admitted fact that the petitioner was not working as a Managing Director of the Tilam Sangh on 15.09.1995 when the sample was taken by the Food Inspector, the trial court has erred in taking cognizance against the petitioner vide order dated 04.08.2012.
Hence, this criminal misc. petition is allowed and the impugned order dated 04.08.2012 passed in criminal reference No.540/2003 by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhilwara is set aside.

(VIJAY BISHNOI)J. Gaurav Khem Raj vs State on 10 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125504913/
